fields.v: Hassanzadeh Aliabadi, H. (2026). Lessons Outlive Their Failures: A Case Study of Rules for AI Coding Agents. arXiv:2610.32578v1 [cs.SE], 23 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2610.32578v1 [cs.SE]; no venue stated
Independent researcher (single author, personal gmail address)

Evaluates; secondary: Compares — exploratory autobiographical single-case study (six weeks) of the author's own harness of rule files, skills, hooks and lint checks: failure ledger of 118 failures, test of an LLM documentation audit on three models against a 67-item key, counterfactual replay of five past fixes (with vs without fix; across models)
fields.why: The stated contributions are the ledger, the audit test and the replay (p. 2), which fits Evaluates/Compares. But the evaluated harness is the author's own, a public template is released (p. 13) and the Discussion proposes replay-based lesson retirement (p. 11), so 'Proposes an approach' (which would make Q13 apply) is defensible; author to decide

fields.v: No named SDD approach. The author's personal agent harness (no version; public stripped template at github.com/avtak/divan): AGENTS.md always-loaded rule file + deadlines hook, 11 on-demand SKILL.md workflow skills (incl. focus-guard), pre-tool guard.py hook, post-edit coupled.py hook (Claude Code only), pre-commit lint.py with 17 checks, monthly read-only LLM documentation audit; add-only lesson loop

AGENTS.md (always loaded, size-capped by lint from Day 14); nested directory AGENTS.md files; SKILL.md files; DEADLINES.md table; hook scripts (guard.py, coupled.py); lint.py checks; area change logs recording each failure and fix with its reason

Harness stages by lifecycle: (1) session start: AGENTS.md + deadlines hook; (2) on-demand skills; (3) pre-tool guard; (4) post-edit reminder; (5) pre-commit lint; (6) monthly LLM doc audit (reports only). Lesson loop: failure noticed -> incident logged with reason -> author approval gate promotes a prose rule or code check; no retirement of lessons
Author approval required for any edit to a rule file, skill or check ('records are appended, rules are asked'); author approval gate in the lesson loop; audit reports read by the author
Single artefacts / harness components in daily use (rule file, skills, hooks, lint checks, LLM audit); not an SDD workflow. Replay tests individual fixes (2 lint checks, 1 hook, 2 prose rules)
Not classifiable (rule files and harness, no specification)
Existing code base: a private personal repository of plain markdown and small Python scripts (system of record for job search, language learning, admin), edited daily by agents

929 commits by 15 Oct 2026 (336 automated sync); study window 912 commits; 118 failures; rule text 4,921 to 17,366 words; replay 30 runs on Sonnet 5.5 + cross-model runs; audit 9 runs on a 67-item key
Personal knowledge / documentation repository (markdown + Python), not a software product
Single user (the author), three agent runtimes (Claude Code and Antigravity on a laptop, headless server agent)
Not measured systematically; replay of 30 headless sessions took 10 minutes and about $3.55 in API-equivalent tokens (reported in Discussion)
Failure occurrence per replay condition (runs in which the failure occurred, x of 3); audit recall on 47 real stale statements and 20 planted errors; audit precision

Failure ledger: 118 failures by category, fix type and recurrence (Recurred / Did not / Unknown); daily word count of rule text; guardrail firings from 74 session transcripts (blocked commands); inter-pass agreement (Cohen's kappa) of the coding

Ledger: keyword filter + LLM extraction (Claude Sonnet 5.5) from git log, change logs, audit reports and diary; blind second coding pass (Claude Opus 5.5); disagreements resolved by author; 30-row manual check. Word counts by script over git history. Audit scored against the key by an Opus 5.5 evaluation pass, spot-checked and reviewed by the author. Replay outcomes counted per run. Guardrail counts parsed from transcripts

(1) LLM doc audit (headless read-only agent, fixed prompt; runtime not named), 3 runs each, criterion: recall vs 67-item key (47 real + 20 planted), precision: Haiku 5.5: real drift 26.2% mean (7-18 items), planted 65.0%; quality: does not work (finds about a quarter of real drift). Sonnet 5.5: real drift 49.6% (22-25 items; 63.8% pooled over 3 runs), planted 80.0%; quality: partly. Opus 5.5 (Haiku subagents): real drift 41.1% (16-21), planted 83.3%; quality: partly. Precision 0.93-1.00 per run over all nine runs (8 false alarms). Cost: not reported for any audit run. (2) Replay on Claude Code + Sonnet 5.5, 3 runs per condition, criterion: runs in which the failure occurs. Condition B (harness with fix): stale skill counts (lint Check 12) 0/2, 1 declined: quality works; superseded decision (prose rule) 0/3: works, but failure also absent without the rule; em-dash (lint Check 9) 0/3: works, check never exercised; destructive reset (guard.py) 0/3: works, guard never exercised; run-time estimate (prose rule): declined in all 3, no measurement. Condition A (harness without the fix): stale counts 3/3: does not work; superseded 0/3, em-dash 0/3, reset 0/3: works; estimate declined. (3) Cross-model replay (3 runs per cell), em-dash A/B and estimate A/B: Claude Code + Sonnet 4.5: em-dash 1/3 (A: partly), 0/3 (B: works); estimate 2/3, 2/3 (prose rule does not work). Claude Code + Sonnet 5: em-dash 0/3, 0/3 (one em-dash in B caught by lint: works); estimate declined (no measurement). Claude Code + Sonnet 5.5: 0/3, 0/3 (works); estimate declined. Antigravity + Gemini 3.8 Flash (medium): em-dash 0/3, 0/3 (works); estimate 0/2, 0/1 executed runs (works, few runs). Cost verdict for all replay entries: not reported (only total ~$3.55 for 30 Sonnet 5.5 replay runs, 10 minutes)

Replay: five past failures with a triggering task and self-contained fix commit; two throwaway git clones per failure (A: state just before fix; B: same state + fix cherry-picked), same neutral commit message; tasks run headless 3 times per condition on Sonnet 5.5 (30 runs); em-dash and estimate scenarios repeated on Sonnet 4.5, Sonnet 5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash. Held constant: repository state, task, model within cell. Audit: isolated clone at commit 769dc91, 3 runs x 3 models, fixed prompt, planted files hidden with skip-worktree. Acceptance criterion: failure occurrence judged per run; audit vs answer key. Repetitions: 3. Human intervention: headless, none stated during runs. Confound: host clock made deadlines look imminent, focus rule declined 7 of 30 Sonnet 5.5 runs

Only the stale-count failure recurred without its fix (3/3) and was stopped by the lint check (0/2); one-sided Fisher p = 0.10, not significant. Three other finished scenarios did not occur with or without fix on Sonnet 5.5. Prose estimate rule made no difference on Sonnet 4.5 (2/3 vs 2/3). Audit: Sonnet 5.5 best on real drift (49.6% vs Opus 41.1%, Haiku 26.2%); planted errors Opus 83.3% > Sonnet 80.0% > Haiku 65.0%; no significance tests. Planted-error detection by kind: cron 100%, identifiers 93%, paths 80%, rules 78%, counts 72%, script behaviour 33%, deadline 33%

Partly: distinguished the stale-count lint check; for em-dash and reset scenarios the trigger was never reached, so they do not test whether the lesson is needed; estimate scenario on Sonnet 5.5 gave no measurement (focus rule declined). Repeatability: 3 runs per cell. Limitations stated: few runs; LLMs as measuring tools; reconstructed prompts may miss original triggers; original incidents on other models; host clock confound (propose libfaketime)

Single-user system designed and studied by the author (no statistical generalisation); researcher roles and expectation bias; recall of the keyword search not measured; under-reporting (chat corrections not logged); six-week window, one heavy audit day (35 drift incidents on 14 Oct; without it drift 13 of 83); answer key under-counts drift (9 extra found). Gaps: no tool retires obsolete lessons after model upgrades; propose recording model version per lesson, re-test dates, automated lesson retirement by replay, regression checks before new lessons go live
